thread:
Ivy Park: uploaded a concept for an 'Egress simulator' in the on-prem setup wizard  allows users to run a single simulated request out to a chosen endpoint and get a human-readable cause + suggested fixes. figma: https://figma.com/file/egress-sim

Ravi Desai: love the idea. helps reduce back-and-forth with infra. question: should simulator run by default when a host is added, or be opt-in? my vote: opt-in, with a lightweight quick-check auto-run on collapse.

Maya Lopez: agree opt-in. copy suggestion for CTA: `Simulate outbound request` (primary) and `Quick check` (secondary). Quick check runs cheap TCP/DNS probes; simulate runs an actual HTTP/HTTPS request with headers masked.

Lin Gomez: accessibility note: results must be exposed as a clear plain-language summary first, then technical details. use `role=status aria-live=polite` for the top-line outcome. include sr-only prefixes like "Simulation result: Success" or "Simulation result: Blocked" before any icons.

Ivy Park: UX detail: show three result tiers: Success (green), Partial (amber, e.g., TLS handshake ok but 403), and Blocked (red). each tier has a short one-line explanation and an expandable `See diagnostic steps` that provides commands and suggested firewall/proxy edits.

Ravi Desai: implementation note: simulated request should replace sensitive headers with `X-Redwood-Sim: true` and never send authentication tokens. also timeout at 6s and surface cURL and telnet snippets in the diagnostic panel. e.g., `curl -I https://storage.redwood.ai/health` and `nc -vz host 443`.

Maya Lopez: copy microcopy: success line `Outbound request succeeded  200 OK` partial `Handshake ok  403 Forbidden` blocked `Connection refused or timed out` plus `Suggested fixes` link. keep short.

Lin Gomez: keyboard flow: simulator control is a modal. when launched, focus moves to modal. results are inside `role=document` and the summary has `aria-live` updates. `See diagnostic steps` is a button that expands a code region with `aria-expanded` toggles. provide a `Copy all diagnostics` button with visible and sr-only labels.
\
ops-bot: note: long-running simulations (>10s) will be queued and youll get a notification when ready. please avoid running for many hosts in parallel.

Ivy Park: visual idea: show a small timeline below results: `Started  DNS lookup  TLS handshake  Request` with ticks and where it failed. users find it easier to parse than logs. keep it compact for mobile widths.

Ravi Desai: backend: return structured result: `status`, `failed_step`, `raw_logs[]`, `suggested_commands[]` so UI can render summary + details. frontend should map `failed_step` to human copy. we'll default to `Try port 443 outbound` for common failures.

Maya Lopez: testing: draft three example simulations for the mock: 1) success to AWS S3 (200), 2) TLS ok but 403 (auth issue), 3) TCP timeout (egress blocked). I'll add them to figma states.

Lin Gomez: accessibility extras: for colorblind users include distinct icons and an explicit SR string. e.g., `aria-label="Simulation result: Blocked. Step: TCP connect failed."` Also announce next action: "Press Enter to expand steps" for the details button.

Ivy Park: final asks for this pass: 1) three microcopy variants for status lines (Maya), 2) aria snippets & keyboard flows (Lin), 3) API contract skeleton for simulator job (Ravi), 4) figma states (me). will review in design crit tomorrow. thanks! :sparkles:
